title: Car Shipping in Yonkers, NY | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: Car shipping from Yonkers and southern Westchester. Open and enclosed carriers, door-to-door, nationwide. Call our Yonkers Ave office at (914) 785-6974.
heroSub: Door-to-door auto transport for Yonkers, Bronxville, Tuckahoe, Scarsdale, Mount Vernon and the Hudson river towns. Open or enclosed carriers, nationwide, with an instant online quote and a dispatcher who knows which Yonkers streets a truck can climb.
intro:
Car shipping in Yonkers starts with the hills. The city climbs from the Hudson at Getty Square up through Park Hill, Nodine Hill and Ludlow to the ridge along Central Park Avenue, and a loaded 75-foot hauler does not want to crawl up Ashburton Avenue or back down Ludlow Street with eight cars on its back. Our office at 570 Yonkers Ave #350, across from Empire City Casino and the old Yonkers Raceway grounds, sits on the flat eastern side of the city where the trucks actually run, and that is no accident.

Yonkers is the gateway between New York City and Westchester, which makes it a convenient first or last stop for carriers working the I-87 corridor. From this office we handle Yonkers auto transport for every neighborhood in the city plus Bronxville, Tuckahoe, Eastchester, Mount Vernon, Scarsdale and the river villages from Hastings-on-Hudson up to Ardsley. Whether you need to ship a car from Yonkers, NY to a condo in Florida or move a family SUV to a new job in Charlotte, the plan below is the one our dispatchers use.

sections.h2: Thruway exits, Central Park Avenue and the parkway problem in Yonkers
sections.html:
Every parkway that touches Yonkers bans commercial trucks: the Saw Mill River, the Sprain Brook, the Bronx River and the Cross County. That leaves car haulers one real artery, the New York State Thruway (I-87), with exits 1 through 6A serving the city from the Bronx line up to Tuckahoe Road and Stew Leonard Drive. A driver coming off the Thruway will typically work Yonkers Avenue, Central Park Avenue (Route 100), Tuckahoe Road, Nepperhan Avenue or McLean Avenue, all of which are legal truck routes with the width to pull over and load.

What this means for you is simple. If your home is within a few blocks of one of those roads, a door-to-door pickup is realistic. If you live up on Nodine Hill, in the narrow blocks of Park Hill off Van Cortlandt Park Avenue, or on the steep streets of Ludlow near the river, the driver will usually ask to meet a short drive away rather than risk the grade with a full load. We tell you this at booking, not on pickup day.

sections.h2: Where haulers meet Yonkers customers: Cross County, Ridge Hill and Empire City
sections.html:
Yonkers has three meeting spots that drivers already know, and we use them constantly.

  • Cross County Shopping Center at the Cross County Parkway and Central Park Avenue. The outer lots have room for a full rig, and the Thruway is two minutes away via Yonkers Avenue.
  • Ridge Hill off Tuckahoe Road and the Sprain Brook, close to Thruway exit 6A. Good for Dunwoodie, Homefield, Crestwood and anyone coming down from Greenburgh.
  • Empire City Casino at Yonkers Raceway, directly across Yonkers Avenue from our office. The large surface lots along Yonkers Avenue and Central Park Avenue are the easiest truck access in the city, and you can walk over to 570 Yonkers Ave #350 if you want to sign paperwork in person.

Meeting the truck at one of these spots usually costs you ten minutes and saves the driver an hour, which is why carriers accept Yonkers loads quickly when we note a flat, accessible handoff point on the order.

sections.h2: Downtown waterfront high-rises and other garage pickups
sections.html:
The buildings along the Hudson in downtown Yonkers, from the towers near the Yonkers Metro-North station to the newer developments along Alexander Street and Warburton Avenue, all keep their cars in structured garages with height limits and no street staging. A car hauler cannot wait on Buena Vista Avenue, and the loading areas are built for moving vans, not open-deck trailers.

For those pickups you drive the car out of the garage and meet the truck a few blocks east on Nepperhan Avenue, or we arrange the Empire City handoff. The same applies to the garage buildings around Mount Vernon West and Fleetwood on the Harlem Line, and to the apartment blocks along Bronx River Road in Bronxville and Tuckahoe. Tell us the building and we will suggest the closest spot where a 10-car carrier can sit legally for twenty minutes.

One low-level note for the river side of town: Warburton Avenue and Riverdale Avenue do see Hudson tidal flooding during strong nor'easters and spring high tides. If a storm is forecast for your pickup window and the car is parked low near the river, we will try to move the date forward rather than have a driver inspect a wet vehicle.

sections.h2: Metro-North, colleges and hospitals: who ships a car from Yonkers
sections.html:
Yonkers auto transport orders follow the train lines and the big local institutions. On the Hudson Line we see customers from Yonkers, Glenwood, Greystone and Ludlow stations; on the Harlem Line it is Mount Vernon West, Fleetwood, Bronxville, Tuckahoe and Crestwood. People move here for the commute and move away when the commute ends, and they usually fly rather than drive.

  • College families. Sarah Lawrence College in Bronxville, Mercy University on the Dobbs Ferry campus and Manhattan College just over the line in Riverdale all generate August and May car moves, typically for students going to or from the South, Midwest and California.
  • Hospital staff. St. John's Riverside on North Broadway and Montefiore New Rochelle rotate residents and traveling nurses who need a car shipped for a one-year placement and then shipped home again.
  • Retirees leaving Westchester. The largest single group. Decades of property tax on a house in Colonial Heights or Bryn Mawr tend to end with a move to Florida, the Carolinas or Tennessee, and the car goes on a truck while the owners close the sale.
  • Corporate relocations out of the White Plains and Greenburgh office parks, usually with the employer paying for enclosed transport.

sections.h2: Enclosed carriers for Scarsdale and Bronxville garages
sections.html:
Southern Westchester has an unusual concentration of cars worth protecting. Scarsdale, Bronxville, Lawrence Park and the estate streets off Pondfield Road hold Porsches, classic Mercedes, Range Rovers and the occasional Ferrari that spends winter in a heated garage and summer in Palm Beach or Naples. For those vehicles we book enclosed, usually a hard-sided trailer with a liftgate so a low front splitter never touches a ramp.

Enclosed runs about 40 to 60 percent above an open carrier on the same lane, and the trucks are smaller, which actually helps on Westchester streets. A 2- or 3-car enclosed rig can get down a Scarsdale cul-de-sac that a 9-car open hauler cannot. For an everyday Honda or Subaru headed to a daughter's apartment in Raleigh, open transport is the right call and what most Yonkers customers choose. Winter is the exception: from December to March, road salt from the Thruway and the Cross County coats everything on an open deck, and some owners of newer cars pay for enclosed just to skip the detailing bill at the other end.

sections.h2: Timing a Yonkers pickup around the Thruway, the casino and the weather
sections.html:
Carriers running the I-87 corridor usually reach Yonkers in the morning after loading in the Bronx or New Jersey, or late afternoon on the way back south. We try to avoid Yonkers Avenue on evening race nights and weekend afternoons when the Empire City lots fill, and we avoid Central Park Avenue near Cross County during the holiday shopping weeks for the same reason.

Weather is a smaller factor here than on Long Island, but hills plus ice is a bad combination. A January storm that leaves Nodine Hill or the Park Hill grades slick will push a pickup a day or two. Most of the year, a Yonkers order placed with a flexible two- or three-day window gets a truck within that window, and the car is in Florida three to four days later.

To get a firm number, use the instant quote form or call the Yonkers Avenue office at (914) 785-6974. Have the pickup address, the destination, the vehicle and whether it runs, and we will tell you which exit the driver will use and where you are likely to meet him.

faqs.q: Can a car hauler come up to my house on Nodine Hill or in Park Hill?
faqs.a: Usually not with a full load. The grades and the parked cars on streets like Elm Street and Oak Street are more than a loaded open hauler should attempt. The driver will call ahead and meet you at the bottom near Nepperhan Avenue or Yonkers Avenue, or in the Empire City lot. Smaller enclosed trucks can sometimes make it; we will tell you which at booking.

faqs.q: Why can't the truck use the Saw Mill or Sprain Brook to reach me?
faqs.a: Both are New York State parkways with commercial vehicle bans and low stone bridges, and the Cross County and Bronx River parkways are the same. A car carrier that tries it gets a ticket or a bridge strike. Every hauler we dispatch comes in on the Thruway and finishes on Central Park Avenue, Tuckahoe Road, Yonkers Avenue or Nepperhan Avenue.

faqs.q: I live in a downtown Yonkers waterfront building with a garage. How does pickup work?
faqs.a: You drive the car out of the garage and meet the driver on a nearby legal stretch, typically Nepperhan Avenue or the Empire City lot a short drive east. The truck cannot stage on Buena Vista or Warburton. Plan on a 20-minute handoff for the inspection and photos, then you walk or ride back. We confirm the spot with the driver the day before.

faqs.q: We are retiring from Bronxville to Florida. How far ahead should we book?
faqs.a: Seven to ten days is comfortable for most of the year. Between late October and mid-December, when a lot of Westchester is doing the same thing, give us two weeks so you are not paying a premium to get on a truck. Transit from Yonkers to the Gulf Coast or Palm Beach County runs three to four days on an open carrier.

faqs.q: Is enclosed shipping worth it for a car coming out of Scarsdale?
faqs.a: For a sports car, a classic, or anything with low clearance, yes. Enclosed rigs are shorter, can reach a tight Scarsdale or Bronxville street, carry a liftgate and keep winter salt off the paint. For a daily driver going to a student in Raleigh or a condo in Naples, open transport is the sensible choice and about 40 to 60 percent cheaper.
